insight.title: Why Your Shopping Cart Is Designed to Wander
insight.subtitle: Its intentionally unruly wheels subtly slow you down and nudge you towards more products.
insight.notificationHook: Shopping carts are designed to drift

sections.text: You push your cart down the aisle, yet it subtly drifts, demanding constant small corrections. That common "pull" to one side, forcing you to adjust, isn't a defect; it's a quiet feature of its design.

Unlike cars, shopping carts use four swivel caster wheels. This allows instant 360-degree pivots in tight spaces. However, it also inherently creates instability for straight-line tracking, leading to that gentle, persistent wander.

This controlled "drifting" subtly slows your pace, making you more attentive to surrounding displays. It encourages a meandering path through aisles, maximizing your exposure to tempting impulse purchases you might otherwise speed past.
A slightly unruly cart keeps your eyes (and wallet) open.
